_comment: panelkit design tokens for the Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-1.8 V2.
Every number here was measured on the device -- nothing is inferred.
One file, two readers: uikit/tokens.py (generators) and tools/simulator/lint.js
(the pre-flash check). Neither redefines a number; change it here or nowhere.

device.note: portrait; the launcher owns the top-edge home gesture

text.note: 16 is an absolute floor, applying to every role. At 368x448 at typical holding distance, desktop text sizing runs at roughly half of what is legible. The floor is 16 rather than 15 because 15 is not on font_ladder and is therefore drawn at 12.
text.font_ladder_note: The ONLY font sizes that exist on this board. CONFIG_LV_USE_FREETYPE and CONFIG_LV_USE_TINY_TTF are both off in examples/system/super/sdkconfig, so the TTFs under /system/fonts are never loaded and every glyph comes from a compiled-in LVGL Montserrat. get_builtin_font() in gui/brookesia_gui_lvgl/src/style_font.cpp returns an exact match or else the closest SMALLER face -- a size off this ladder does not scale, it silently rounds DOWN. That is how the shell's 11sp clock ended up drawn at 8px and how a 56px 'hero' is really 48px. Snap every size to a rung.
text.line_height_note: Real .line_height from each lv_font_montserrat_<n>.c, not a guess. A label box shorter than this clips descenders. Ratio is ~1.1x the nominal size -- eyeballing it as 1.3x (a desktop CSS habit) falsely condemns boxes that are fine and hides the ones that are not.

touch.note: Controls 50-56px tall and 10px apart read as one blob and mis-fire. The gap minimum guards the ambiguity between two discrete, similarly-sized controls; a control that fills its whole hit region needs no gap at all, because there is no ambiguous sliver between it and its neighbour.

color.note: Cloudera orange + the leaderboard medal set, taken from the racing game's own leaderboard.html

note: Trap 1: layout.type flex on a parent silently overrides its children's absolute x/y -- a screen renders near-blank.
Trap 2: requireValidPress drops a tap the finger drifted through, and container defaults to scrollable:true, so a small drag becomes a scroll.

Trap 5: a big tap target inside a swipe surface. LVGL sends ONE gesture per finger-down/up (indev->pointer.gesture_sent latches it), but a tap target under the same finger fires on `pressed` AND on `released` -- so one drag across a half-panel nav zone scored three navigations, in whichever direction the drag STARTED. gesture_target_ratio is the share of a gesture-declaring node's width AND height at which a tap target inside it stops being a control and becomes the drag surface: 1/3 of each. A small control (a toolbar button) is fine; a half-panel zone is not. Found in #220 -- it is why tunastreet.tminus and tunastreet.xviewer navigate by swipe alone.

safe_area.note: The glass is a ROUNDED rectangle, so the usable width near the top and bottom edges is narrower than 368. Text placed at the nominal 16px edge inset but only a few pixels down is inside the corner arc and reads as jammed into the curve, or is physically cut. Required inset at vertical distance d from the edge is R - sqrt(R^2 - (R-d)^2). At d=2 with R=52 that is 39px.
safe_area.calibration: corner_radius is an ESTIMATE. It is in no board yaml, datasheet or driver in this tree -- nothing on the device reports it. 52 is deliberately on the generous side: over-inset costs a few pixels, under-inset is a visible defect. To calibrate, change this ONE number and regenerate -- everything downstream (lint R10, panelkit.corner_inset) reads it from here.
